# 2324     "# # # #  🔍 What this code does:\n",
# 2325     "- The code groups log entries (`provider_log`) by their `called_by_type` (who invoked them) and `provider_type` (what kind of provider was called).\n",
# 2326     "- It then builds a flow network showing how control moves from one provider type to the next.\n",
# 2327     "- The width of each band represents the number of calls made along that path.\n",
# 2328     "\n",
# 2329     "# # # #  🧠 What you're seeing in the chart:\n",
# 2330     "- **Left-to-right flow** from high-level providers like `session`, `program`, and `controller`, down to mid-level like `system` and `state`, and finally to low-level workers like `agent`, `score`, and `tool`.\n",
# 2331     "- **Wider bands** indicate more frequent interactions. For example, the `state → score` and `score → tool` flows are thick, indicating heavy evaluation and tool usage.\n",
# 2332     "- **Branching paths** (e.g., from `agent` to `score`, `tool`, `agent_engine`) reveal the dependencies that agents rely on to make decisions.\n",

# 3193     "import plotly.graph_objects as go\n",
# 3194     "\n",
# 3195     "#  Prepare nodes and links\n",
# 3196     "df[\"source\"] = df[\"called_by_type\"].fillna(\"start\")\n",
# 3197     "df[\"target\"] = df[\"provider_type\"]\n",
# 3198     "\n",
# 3199     "nodes = list(set(df[\"source\"]) | set(df[\"target\"]))\n",
# 3200     "node_indices = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(nodes)}\n",
# 3201     "\n",
# 3202     "link_data = (\n",
# 3203     "    df.groupby([\"source\", \"target\"])\n",
# 3204     "    .size()\n",
# 3205     "    .reset_index(name=\"count\")\n",
# 3206     "    .assign(\n",
# 3207     "        source_idx=lambda d: d[\"source\"].map(node_indices),\n",
# 3208     "        target_idx=lambda d: d[\"target\"].map(node_indices)\n",
# 3209     "    )\n",
# 3210     ")\n",
# 3211     "\n",
# 3212     "fig = go.Figure(go.Sankey(\n",
# 3213     "    node=dict(\n",
# 3214     "        pad=15,\n",
# 3215     "        thickness=20,\n",
# 3216     "        line=dict(color=\"black\", width=0.5),\n",
# 3217     "        label=nodes\n",
# 3218     "    ),\n",
# 3219     "    link=dict(\n",
# 3220     "        source=link_data[\"source_idx\"],\n",
# 3221     "        target=link_data[\"target_idx\"],\n",
# 3222     "        value=link_data[\"count\"]\n",
# 3223     "    )\n",
# 3224     "))\n",
# 3225     "\n",

# 5049     "# # #  📦 Treemap of Provider Execution Cost\n",
# 5050     "\n",
# 5051     "This chart presents a **latency-weighted treemap** that reveals the **nested execution structure** of a CodeCritic run — from top-level orchestration down to fine-grained tooling.\n",
# 5052     "\n",
# 5053     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 5054     "- **Builds a call hierarchy** by tracing each provider’s `called_by_type`, recursively reconstructing the execution path for every log entry.\n",
# 5055     "- **Flattens each path** into separate columns (e.g., `path_0`, `path_1`, ...) so Plotly can visualize the full call stack as a nested tree.\n",
# 5056     "- **Visualizes latency cost** using a treemap, where:\n",
# 5057     "  - Each **box** represents a provider type at a specific nesting level.\n",
# 5058     "  - **Box size** is proportional to total `latency_ms` contributed by that node and its descendants.\n",
# 5059     "  - **Color** corresponds to `provider_type`, using a colorblind-safe palette.\n",
# 5060     "\n",
# 5061     "# # # #  🔍 What you're observing:\n",
# 5062     "- The **upper-left boxes** show top-level orchestrators (e.g., `session`, `program`).\n",
# 5063     "- As you move inward (right and down), you see **nested calls** to `controller`, `system`, `state`, and ultimately `agent`, `tool`, `score`, etc.\n",
# 5064     "- **Larger boxes** deeper in the tree indicate subsystems that consume significant time (e.g., tools like `mypy`, `black`, `ruff`).\n",
# 5065     "- Hovering on a box reveals its exact path and latency.\n",
# 5066     "\n",
# 5067     "This visualization is ideal for:\n",
# 5068     "- Identifying where latency accumulates in multi-step workflows.\n",
# 5069     "- Spotting repeated or redundant calls.\n",

# 6099     "import plotly.express as px\n",
# 6100     "\n",
# 6101     "#  Step 1: Build edges and infer nesting path\n",
# 6102     "df[\"source\"] = df[\"called_by_type\"].fillna(\"root\")\n",
# 6103     "df[\"target\"] = df[\"provider_type\"]\n",
# 6104     "edges = list(zip(df[\"source\"], df[\"target\"]))\n",
# 6105     "\n",
# 6106     "#  Recursive path builder\n",
# 6107     "def build_path(row, edges):\n",
# 6108     "    if row[\"source\"] == \"root\":\n",
# 6109     "        return [\"root\", row[\"target\"]]\n",
# 6110     "    for src, tgt in edges:\n",
# 6111     "        if tgt == row[\"source\"]:\n",
# 6112     "            return build_path({\"source\": src, \"target\": tgt}, edges) + [row[\"target\"]]\n",
# 6113     "    return [\"root\", row[\"source\"], row[\"target\"]]\n",
# 6114     "\n",
# 6115     "df[\"call_path\"] = df.apply(lambda row: build_path(row, edges), axis=1)\n",
# 6116     "\n",
# 6117     "#  Step 2: Flatten call path into real columns\n",
# 6118     "path_df = df[\"call_path\"].apply(pd.Series)\n",
# 6119     "path_df.columns = [f\"path_{i}\" for i in path_df.columns]\n",
# 6120     "\n",
# 6121     "#  Step 3: Combine into sunburst data source\n",
# 6122     "path_df = path_df.fillna(\"\")\n",
# 6123     "\n",
# 6124     "#  Then proceed as before\n",
# 6125     "sunburst_data = pd.concat([df, path_df], axis=1)\n",
# 6126     "\n",
# 6127     "\n",
# 6128     "fig = px.treemap(\n",
# 6129     "    sunburst_data,\n",
# 6130     "    path=path_df.columns.tolist(),\n",

# 6144     "# # #  🗺️ Provider Flow by Actor Type (One Node per Provider)\n",
# 6145     "\n",
# 6146     "This directed graph visualizes the **execution flow between unique providers** involved in a single run.\n",
# 6147     "\n",
# 6148     "# # # #  🧠 What this code does:\n",
# 6149     "- Extracts all log entries that include a `file_name`, sorted by time.\n",
# 6150     "- Groups logs by unique `(provider_type, provider_id)` pairs to ensure **each provider appears only once**.\n",
# 6151     "- Builds a directed graph showing **execution order** from one provider to the next.\n",
# 6152     "- Colors each node by `provider_type` (e.g. `system`, `state`, `agent`, `tool`) using a consistent palette.\n",
# 6153     "- Labels nodes as `<provider_type> (ID <provider_id>)`, making it easy to trace control flow.\n",
# 6154     "\n",
# 6155     "# # # #  🔍 What you're observing:\n",
# 6156     "- **Nodes** represent provider instances (e.g., `agent (ID 2)`, `tool (ID 1)`).\n",
# 6157     "- **Edges** represent transitions between providers during file processing, preserving execution order.\n",
# 6158     "- The layout is **stable** using a fixed seed, so it won't change between runs.\n",
# 6159     "- Helps reveal **which components are chained**, reused, or terminal in the flow.\n",
# 6160     "\n",
# 6161     "This visualization is especially useful for understanding how files propagate through an FSM-controlled execution graph, and for debugging orchestration logic.\n"
# 6162    ]
# 6163   },

# 6182     "import networkx as nx\n",
# 6183     "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
# 6184     "\n",
# 6185     "#  Sort and dedupe by provider (only first appearance matters here)\n",
# 6186     "df_files = df[df[\"file_name\"].notna()].sort_values(\"timestamp\").copy()\n",
# 6187     "df_files = df_files[[\"timestamp\", \"provider_type\", \"provider_id\", \"file_name\"]].drop_duplicates()\n",
# 6188     "df_files[\"node\"] = df_files.apply(lambda row: f\"{row['provider_type']} (ID {row['provider_id']})\", axis=1)\n",
# 6189     "\n",
# 6190     "#  One row per provider node\n",
# 6191     "df_nodes = df_files.drop_duplicates(subset=[\"node\"]).reset_index(drop=True)\n",
# 6192     "\n",
# 6193     "#  Build node color mapping\n",
# 6194     "provider_types = df_nodes[\"provider_type\"].unique()\n",
# 6195     "color_map = dict(zip(provider_types, plt.get_cmap(\"tab10\").colors[:len(provider_types)]))\n",
# 6196     "node_colors = df_nodes[\"provider_type\"].map(color_map)\n",
# 6197     "\n",
# 6198     "#  Build edges between nodes (based on execution order)\n",
# 6199     "edges = []\n",
# 6200     "for i in range(1, len(df_nodes)):\n",
# 6201     "    prev = df_nodes.iloc[i - 1]\n",
# 6202     "    curr = df_nodes.iloc[i]\n",
# 6203     "    edges.append((prev[\"node\"], curr[\"node\"], curr[\"file_name\"]))\n",
# 6204     "\n",
# 6205     "#  Create graph\n",
# 6206     "G = nx.DiGraph()\n",
# 6207     "for src, tgt, label in edges:\n",
# 6208     "    G.add_edge(src, tgt, label=\"file\")\n",
# 6209     "\n",
# 6210     "#  Draw with color\n",
# 6211     "plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))\n",
# 6212     "pos = nx.spring_layout(G, k=0.6, seed=32)  #  🔒 fixed layout\n",
# 6213     "\n",
# 6214     "nx.draw(\n",
# 6215     "    G, pos,\n",
# 6216     "    with_labels=True,\n",
# 6217     "    labels={node: node for node in G.nodes},\n",
# 6218     "    node_color=node_colors,\n",
# 6219     "    node_size=2000,\n",
# 6220     "    edge_color='gray',\n",
# 6221     "    arrows=True,\n",
# 6222     "    font_size=10\n",
# 6223     ")\n",
# 6224     "\n",
# 6225     "nx.draw_networkx_edge_labels(\n",
# 6226     "    G, pos,\n",
# 6227     "    edge_labels=nx.get_edge_attributes(G, 'label'),\n",
# 6228     "    font_size=8\n",

# 9722     "import plotly.express as px\n",
# 9723     "\n",
# 9724     "#  Compute total latency and count\n",
# 9725     "latency_stats = (\n",
# 9726     "    df.groupby(\"provider_type\")[\"latency_ms\"]\n",
# 9727     "    .agg(total_latency=\"sum\", call_count=\"count\")\n",
# 9728     "    .reset_index()\n",
# 9729     ")\n",
# 9730     "\n",
# 9731     "#  Calculate average latency per call\n",
# 9732     "latency_stats[\"avg_latency_per_call\"] = latency_stats[\"total_latency\"] / latency_stats[\"call_count\"]\n",
# 9733     "\n",
# 9734     "#  Convert label values to integers for display\n",
# 9735     "latency_stats[\"avg_latency_label\"] = latency_stats[\"avg_latency_per_call\"].round().astype(int)\n",
# 9736     "\n",
# 9737     "#  Sort for visual clarity\n",
# 9738     "latency_stats = latency_stats.sort_values(\"avg_latency_per_call\", ascending=False)\n",
# 9739     "\n",
# 9740     "#  Plot\n",
# 9741     "fig = px.bar(\n",
# 9742     "    latency_stats,\n",
# 9743     "    x=\"provider_type\",\n",
# 9744     "    y=\"avg_latency_per_call\",\n",
# 9745     "    text=\"avg_latency_label\",\n",
# 9746     "    title=\"⏱️ Average Latency per Call by Provider Type\",\n",
# 9747     "    labels={\"provider_type\": \"Provider Type\", \"avg_latency_per_call\": \"Avg Latency (ms)\"},\n",
# 9748     "    color=\"provider_type\",\n",
# 9749     "    color_discrete_sequence=px.colors.qualitative.Set2\n",
# 9750     ")\n",
# 9751     "fig.update_traces(textposition=\"outside\")\n",
